messages:
Elena (CS): Dropping a tiny 'Priming Bridge' handoff for accounts flagged on the renewal-watchlist. Objective: preload hot routes, stagger priming to avoid spikes, collect failure artifacts for QA, and provide a short deterministic degrade. Keep it short & copy/paste.
Max (FieldOps): Please include exact commands our infra team can run during the maintenance window and a 3-item on-call checklist.
Elena (CS): Got it. Pasteable plan below (for your runbook). 3 phases + on-call checklist.
Phase 1 — Preload (T-30m): seed hot routes
- Run 3 unique preload requests (different prompts) against top 5 endpoints to populate KV/cache. Example command (run from CI):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Preload: welcome","max_tokens":20,"mode":"preload"}'
```
- Quick probe to verify cache applied: GET /v0/health/preload -> returns something like {"preload_ok":true,"cache_hits":N} (probe off by default for security).
Phase 2 — Staggered ramp (T0 to T+60m): conservative shaping
- Apply safe config (copy/paste):
```
{ "preload": true, "preload_ttl_sec": 300, "max_preload_concurrency": 3, "batch_window_ms": 30, "stream_abort_ms": 750, "auto_disable_err_pct": 0.07 }
```
- Ramp schedule: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 8min observation windows. If error_rate >= 6% or p95 > 800ms at any step, pause and run fallback.
Phase 3 — Stabilize & capture (T+1h to 48h): evidence collection
- Keep preload TTL for 24h, collect one slow trace and one failed output every 12h, tag traces with `cs:priming_bridge:<acct>`. Attach failures to shared ticket for QA.
Fallback (instant): deterministic degrade
- Set `preload=false`, set `batch_window_ms=120`, route to `fallback_model:quant-lite-v1` for 90s, enqueue requests for async processing, open incident `priming-bridge-fallback-<acct>`.
On-call checklist (3 items, copyable):
1) Run preload commands T-30m (3 prompts).
2) Apply safe config before traffic shift; step ramp, observe metrics.
3) If errors/fallback: run fallback actions, collect traces, notify customer, tag ticket `priority:renewal-watch`.
Tasha (SRE): Ops tips: add `max_preload_concurrency=3` to protect control plane and `preload_backoff_ms=200` to avoid retry storms. Auto-disable preload when error_rate >= 0.06. Provide a minimal health endpoint for FieldOps to probe (off by default):
```
GET /v0/health/preload_status -> {"status":"ok","last_preload":"2026-03-22T12:34:56Z","cache_hits":N}
```
Ivy (Solutions): For customer enablement calls, deliver a 12-prompt sample pack (8 happy-path, 3 edge, 1 adversarial). Ask customers to run the 3 preload commands using their top 3 prompts and paste outputs to the ticket. Also request 8 failure exemplars for Eval.
QA Bot: REMINDER: tag traces with `cs:priming_bridge` and include `cs:renewal-watch` for any fallback incidents so reporting picks them up.
Max (FieldOps): Can we have a short incident blurb customers can paste? They prefer deterministic language.
Elena (CS): Incident blurb you can paste into the ticket: "Account <acct> — Priming Bridge fallback at <ts>. Actions: disabled preload, switched to `quant-lite-v1`, increased batch_window_ms to 120, inputs queued for async. Attached: slow-trace.zip, failures.json. Please triage with SRE."
Max (FieldOps): Perfect. I'll run T-30m preload in our window and report back with probe outputs.
Elena (CS): I'll post a 1-pager + prompt pack into onboarding-kit and tag the ticket `cs:priming_bridge_2026`. Closing thread.
